spec.title: User applications on native Windows (PROP-059) — ZIP install, launchers, proxies, shell, storage

p.purpose: **Purpose.** The Linux fixtures prove the application subsystem's logic (install, launch, proxies, alternatives, storage, source builds). Windows differs in what no fixture reaches from Linux: the ZIP method and its payload layout, the `.exe` proxy copies in `opt\bin`, direct native launch of `gvim.exe` without an intermediate `cmd`, `Ctrl+C` through the proxy, `vibe shell` reusing `cmd.exe` / PowerShell / `pwsh`, and a removable drive as a storage library. The owner proves these here, on a real Windows machine (`PROP-059#acceptance`).

p.isolation-note: Every step runs against an isolated settings root (`VIBE_SETTINGS`), so the operator's real `~\.vibe` is never touched. Vim's upstream ZIP (about 15 MB) is downloaded once.

facts.PRE-HOST: Windows 10/11 x86_64 with PowerShell and `cmd.exe`; network access to github.com.
facts.PRE-BINARIES: `cargo build -p vibe-cli --bins` on the machine: `target\debug\vibe.exe` AND `target\debug\vibe-app-proxy.exe` beside it (the proxy image is copied into `opt\bin` for every public command).
facts.PRE-PACKAGE: The Vim bridge `org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0` is resolvable: either published to the registry, or a checkout of `vibevm-packages/vim` laid out as `<reg>\org.vibevm.apps\vim\v1.1.0\` and passed with `--registry <reg>`.
facts.PRE-DRIVE: Optional for step 7: a removable drive (USB stick) with a free directory.

section.title: Steps

p.EXP-1: **Expected.** A JSON listing whose `detected` names `windows` / `x86_64`, the `windows` platform first and marked detected, with installer `windows-zip` (type `zip`) and launchers `gvim` (default) and `vim`; the Ubuntu and source-build rows are listed but not detected. Nothing is downloaded and `$env:VIBE_SETTINGS` holds no `applications\index.json` yet.

p.EXP-2: **Expected.** The ZIP is fetched and its SHA-256 verified; the payload (`vim92\gvim.exe`, `vim92\vim.exe`, `vim92\vim.ico`, the runtime tree) sits under `opt\apps\vim\org.vibevm.apps.vim@1.1.0\` because `payload_root = "vim"` selected the archive's `vim\` subtree. `opt\bin` holds `vim.exe` and `gvim.exe`, each a byte copy of `vibe-app-proxy.exe`. The summary line names the installation and `windows-zip`. `applications\index.json` has protocol `vibe-user-applications/3`, one installation with `library: "default"` and `portable: true`, and slot `vim` defaulting to it.

section.fence: & $vibe app launchers org.vibevm.apps/vim & $vibe app start org.vibevm.apps/vim & $vibe app run org.vibevm.apps/vim vim -- --version

p.EXP-3: **Expected.** Both launchers are `available` with resolved absolute paths inside the payload and the `.ico` resolved; `gvim` is marked default. `app start` opens a gVim window directly (Task Manager shows `gvim.exe` as a child of `vibe.exe`, no `cmd.exe` in between); closing it returns 0. `app run … vim -- --version` prints the Vim 9.2 banner in the console and exits 0.

section.fence: & "$env:VIBE_SETTINGS\opt\bin\vim.exe" --version & "$env:VIBE_SETTINGS\opt\bin\vim.exe" # interactive: type :q<Enter> & "$env:VIBE_SETTINGS\opt\bin\vim.exe" # interactive: press Ctrl+C, then :q<Enter>

p.EXP-4: **Expected.** The proxy starts console Vim in the same console with no intermediate shell; `--version` prints the banner. In the interactive runs Vim owns the console, `Ctrl+C` is seen by Vim (it shows `Type :qa and press <Enter>…`, the proxy does not die), and `:q` returns to PowerShell with exit 0. The proxy never prints anything of its own on success.

p.EXP-5: **Expected.** From Windows PowerShell the child is `powershell.exe`; from `pwsh` it is `pwsh.exe`; from `cmd.exe` it is `cmd.exe` (the parent image is reused). Inside, the first PATH entry is `$env:VIBE_SETTINGS\opt\bin`, `vim --version` works through the proxy, and `exit` returns to the caller with the shell's own exit status. `vibe shell --json` and `vibe shell --unattended` are refused before any shell starts.

facts.STEP-6-SESSION: **Session choice (`VIBE_APP_USE`) with a second provider.** Install a second provider of the same slot — the published `org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.0.1` is one — then:

section.fence: & $vibe app alternatives vim & $vibe app use vim org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.0.1 $env:VIBE_APP_USE = "vim=org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0"; vim --version; Remove-Item Env:VIBE_APP_USE

p.EXP-6: **Expected.** `alternatives` lists both providers, the default, and `vim` / `gvim` with the providers offering them. `app use` moves the global default; the session variable overrides it for that process only, and the next `vim --version` without the variable follows the global default again.

facts.STEP-7-STORAGE: **A removable drive as a library; unavailability; move.** With a USB drive `E:`:

section.fence: & $vibe storage add E:\vibe-apps --id usb & $vibe storage move org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 --to usb vim --version # eject / unplug the drive & $vibe app list vim --version; $LASTEXITCODE & $vibe uninstall -g org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 # plug the drive back in & $vibe app list & $vibe storage move org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 --to default & $vibe storage gc

p.EXP-7: **Expected.** `storage add` creates `E:\vibe-apps\vibe-library.toml` and lists `usb`. The move copies the payload to `E:\vibe-apps\apps\vim\…`, rewrites the index and deletes the old directory; `vim --version` still works through the unchanged proxy. With the drive gone, `app list` shows the installation `unavailable` with the reason (library directory missing), `vim.exe` exits 127 with one `vibe-app-proxy: unavailable: …` line, and `uninstall -g` is refused without touching anything. After re-plugging, `app list` shows `ready` with no other command; the move back succeeds, and `gc` reports nothing unreferenced.

p.EXP-8: **Expected.** The payload directory is deleted; with another provider still installed the slot default moves to it and the proxies stay; after the last provider is removed `opt\bin\vim.exe` and `gvim.exe` are gone and `opt\bin` keeps any unrelated file (the version-manager shims).

facts.STEP-9-REQUIREMENT: **A source build that requires a toolchain package (PROP-065 `#app-dependencies`, `#uninstall-tree`).** The Vim bridge's `windows-source` option declares `requires = ["org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@^15.2"]` on its build step and `needs = ["command:gcc"]`; the host has no `gcc` on PATH.

section.fence: & $vibe app plan org.vibevm.apps/vim --installer windows-source & $vibe install -g org.vibevm.apps/vim --installer windows-source --unattended Get-ChildItem "$env:VIBE_SETTINGS\opt\bin" & $vibe app list & $vibe shell --with org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64 # inside: gcc --version; exit & $vibe uninstall -g org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 & $vibe app autoremove

p.EXP-9: **Expected.** The plan shows `dependency: install org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@15.2.0 (build, hidden)` ahead of the build step and does not refuse the `command:gcc` need. The install first installs MinGW hidden (no `gcc.exe` in `opt\bin`, `app list` shows it under "hidden installation(s)" marked `[auto]` and required by Vim), then runs the build with MinGW's `bin` and `gcc` first on the build step's PATH, and leaves only `vim.exe` / `gvim.exe` in `opt\bin`. `vibe shell --with` puts `gcc` on that session's PATH only. Uninstalling Vim lists MinGW as an orphan without removing it; `app autoremove` removes it with its payload.

p.pass-criteria: Every step reads as described on a real Windows host: ZIP install, direct native launch of gVim, console Vim through the `.exe` proxy with Ctrl+C handled by Vim, `vibe shell` reusing each of the three parent shells, the session variable, the removable-drive library with unavailability and moves, and a clean uninstall. The owner signs the date below.

facts.SIGNOFF-OWNER: [ ] Owner sign-off on native Windows (date / initials): ______
facts.EVIDENCE-2026-10-31: **Automated run of 2026-10-31 on `base` (Windows 11, pwsh 7.6, vibe `50a6685cc`, local registry copy of the packages, isolated `VIBE_SETTINGS`).** Steps 1, 2, 4 (`--version` through the proxy), 7 (move to `C:\opt\vibe-apps-final`), 8 and 9 ran as described: the plan listed `dependency: install org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@15.2.0 (build, hidden) … for step build`; the source install took 156 s with no `gcc` on the host PATH and left only `vim.exe` in `opt\bin`; `app list` showed MinGW under hidden installations as `[auto] required by org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0`; `expose` wrote `gcc.exe`, `hide` removed it (and, per PROP-065 `#uninstall-tree`, made the mark `manual`, so the later uninstall listed no orphan — `app mark auto` followed by `app autoremove --plan-only` / `autoremove` showed and removed it as `orphan`); `outdated` reported both current; `uninstall --plan-only` printed the removal plan; run records survived the removal. Interactive steps 3, 5, 6 and the removable drive of 7 remain the owner's.
